what: Clip each tensor's gradient norm against an exponential moving average of its own past clipped norms instead of one global norm
problem_here: Reference says nothing new on clipping and recommends only logging pre-clip norm and clipped fraction; global clipping can hide a too-high LR
mechanism: Per-tensor thresholds follow each tensor's history, so a spike in one layer is cut without shrinking all others
evidence: arXiv 2502.11034 v4 (2026-07-19), ICML 2026, opened abstract: Llama-2 7B, Mixtral 8x1B, ERNIE 10B-A1.4B, spike score 0, +1.32/+1.27/+2.48 points over global clipping, also with Muon and Lion; authors only, code in PaddleFleet, no independent replication seen
maturity: Peer-reviewed conference paper, one group, PaddlePaddle implementation, short runs per a review note
cost: About 20 lines in the training loop and one EMA per tensor; one extra run per arm
simpler_alternative: Keep global-norm clipping and log clipped fraction; lower the LR
reason: Peer-reviewed with released code but single-group evidence and no PyTorch port or replication; the reference sentence saying nothing new exists is wrong either way
cheap_local_trial: On a small model run with an observed loss spike or high clipped fraction, compare global clipping and AdaGC on 3 paired seeds at equal budget; report spike count and final metric against the noise floor

candidate: FP16 trainer and rollout for RL post-training
what: Use FP16 instead of BF16 in both the policy trainer and the rollout engine to shrink the numerical gap between them
problem_here: GRPO runs can destabilise from engine/trainer probability mismatch; reference only logs sampling_logp_difference
mechanism: FP16 has more mantissa bits, so rounding differences between trainer and sampler are smaller
evidence: arXiv 2510.26788 v1 (2025-10-30), opened abstract: mismatch about 24x lower, BF16 GRPO collapsed while FP16 converged; models and scale not on abstract page; no code link; no independent replication found (a search summary that claimed one was wrong)
cost: One extra run per arm; FP16 needs loss scaling and may overflow on some models
simpler_alternative: Keep BF16 and use truncated importance sampling or lower LR
reason: Plausible mechanism and cheap config change, but one source and unread body
cheap_local_trial: Small GRPO run with TRL, BF16 vs FP16, 3 paired seeds; compare sampling_logp_difference, reward curve and collapse count

candidate: Fair Cast unbiased rounding of the bf16 rollout copy
what: Export master weights to the bf16 sampling copy with stochastic rounding or error feedback
problem_here: Round-to-nearest bf16 export may discard most small RL updates so the sampler lags the optimizer
mechanism: Unbiased rounding keeps small updates in expectation
evidence: arXiv 2610.41073 v1 (2026-10-29), opened abstract: Qwen3-0.6B to 4B, 25 seed pairs, 18 wins 6 ties 1 loss, mean +6.1 points; zebra puzzles 0.57 +- 0.16 vs 0.33 +- 0.10 over 4 runs; no code link; no replication
cost: 22 to 38 ms per 1.7B export; small code change in the weight sync
simpler_alternative: Keep fp32 weights for sampling at small scale, or FP16 candidate above
reason: Interesting mechanism but very new, no code, small tasks, no replication
cheap_local_trial: Measure the fraction of served weights that change per step on a small model; only if it is under a few percent run the paired comparison

candidate: Anytime-valid t-test on per-seed differences for staged seed escalation
what: E-process (Wang and Ramdas) on paired or unpaired per-seed score differences so a comparison can go from 3 to 6 seeds without losing error control
problem_here: Reference allows a 3-pair retain only as a candidate and lists staged seed escalation as inferred with no source; a fixed-n keep rule cannot extend sample size
mechanism: Test supermartingale with unknown variance stays valid under optional stopping
evidence: Round 2 (2026-11-12): likelihood-ratio test on the two-sample t statistic, a look after each seed up to 2n, behind the first-seed gate; 200,000 single comparisons (it keeps 61 % of 2-sd gains and 0.8 % of no-effect changes; the built rule 65 % and 2.7 %) and 20,000 campaigns per setting. Design gain 1.5 to 3 sd, keep at 44 or 20; budget 34 runs, 3 seeds; with ideas as the limit it uses 15 to 27 % more runs. Kept with no effect, per idea: 0.25 to 0.79 % against 0.87 %. Before round 2: arXiv 2310.03722 v5 (2024-11-06), Sequential Analysis, opened abstract: closed-form e-process, width polynomial in alpha 'unavoidable'; group-invariance basis Perez-Ortiz et al., Annals of Statistics 2024 (not opened); nothing found on power at n 3 to 6 or on neural-net seeds
maturity: Peer-reviewed theory, no neural-network validation; Python packages savvi and ville exist (not opened)
cost: Small stdlib implementation plus a simulation; likely low power at n = 3
simpler_alternative: Fixed-n unpaired rule with fresh-seed confirmation (already in loop.md) or more seeds up front
reason: Simulated on 12 Nov 2026: over a campaign it loses. With 3.5 to 5 runs per idea a campaign ends at 2.70 to 3.45 against 4.02 (runs limit) or 2.30 to 2.68 against 2.72 (ideas limit), in run-to-run sd. Its gain is fewer false keeps. Reversal: a use where a false keep costs far more than a missed gain.
cheap_local_trial: Simulate normal noise at 3 and 6 seeds: false-keep rate under no effect and detection rate at 2 pooled sd, compared with the loop's rule (2.4% and 44% at 3 seeds)

candidate: Paired seeds as common random numbers
what: Use identical seeds for baseline and candidate and test the per-seed differences
problem_here: uncertainty.md requires paired comparisons but loop.md says seeds did not shift scores consistently, so the loop compares unpaired
mechanism: Variance of the difference falls when the two arms' outcomes are positively correlated across seeds
evidence: Round 2 (2026-11-12): two commits of the benchmark, 8 seeds, 2 repeats, 30 s budget: correlation of the seed means +0.295 (eight seeds need 0.62 to tell it from chance); sd of the per-seed differences 0.0115, against 0.0136 if seeds shared nothing; sd between seeds 0.0106 and 0.0085, between repeats of one seed 0.00013 and 0.0049. Before round 2: arXiv 2512.24145 v3 (2026-01-31), opened: single author, economic simulator, no numbers or code; arXiv 2609.24144 (2026-09-21), opened: paired rollouts need not reduce gradient variance, 3 seeds, learning-curve criterion missed, code TheDeadcoder/paired-rollouts; no neural-network training evidence
maturity: Two single-author preprints outside supervised or LM training
simpler_alternative: Unpaired rule with pooled variance as in loop.md
reason: Measured on the benchmark on 12 Nov 2026: seeds are not common random numbers for two versions of a training script (r = +0.30 between the seed means of two commits over eight seeds). See the note second-look, 'Keep rule that compares a change with the best commit seed by seed'.
cheap_local_trial: From baseline seed panels already in the ledger, split into pseudo-arms and compute the correlation of per-seed scores across arms; adopt pairing only if clearly positive

candidate: Bias-corrected LLM-judge estimates with calibration uncertainty
what: Report judge scores through sensitivity/specificity correction or prediction-powered inference with a human-labelled calibration set
problem_here: Reference adopts no judge and offers only a 30-label correlation gate from one preprint
mechanism: The judge is treated as a noisy surrogate; human labels estimate its bias and the interval includes both test and calibration noise
evidence: arXiv 2511.21140 v4 (2026-05-31), ICML 2026, opened abstract: no numbers or code link on page; arXiv 2601.05420 v1 (2026-01-08), opened: EIF and PPI estimators, code at yiqunchen/debias-llm-as-a-judge, no numbers on the page; no independent replication seen
maturity: Methods papers, one with released code
cost: 30+ human labels and a judge model; network or local judge
simpler_alternative: Exact scorer or human spot checks; no judge
reason: Better-founded than the correlation gate, but no replication and the kit adopts no judge anyway
cheap_local_trial: Pick a task with an exact scorer, treat a small judge as the surrogate on 50 items, and check whether the corrected interval covers the exact score

what: Train linear layers (and for FP4 optimizer states and attention) in 8-bit or 4-bit microscaled formats
problem_here: Reference covers bf16 and TF32 only; throughput and memory levers are limited
mechanism: Lower-precision tensor-core matmuls with block scaling
evidence: arXiv 2509.25149 v2 (2026-03-04), opened: 12B on 10T tokens comparable to FP8, no code or hardware on page; arXiv 2607.04422 v2 (2026-08-07), opened: 3B on 64B tokens, loss gap 0.838% to BF16, no code link; MXFP8 1.2x to 1.3x on B200 from torchao and PyTorch blogs (not opened); no independent replication
maturity: Vendor and single-group results; needs Blackwell-class GPU
cost: Hardware dependent; numerics gate runs; torchao dependency
reason: Vendor-measured speedups on hardware most users lack, short convergence checks, no independent replication
cheap_local_trial: Only if the GPU supports it: end-to-end time-to-target and per-layer gradient norm comparison against bf16 under the performance.md numerics gate

candidate: Batch-invariant ops for reproducible rollouts and evaluation
what: torch.Library overrides for mm, addmm, log_softmax and mean whose results do not depend on batch size
problem_here: Evaluation and RL rollouts can differ with batch size; reference pins batch size and dtype only
mechanism: Fixed reduction order independent of batch composition
evidence: GitHub thinking-machines-lab/batch_invariant_ops README opened: MIT, short supported-op list, inference proof of concept, no training use stated; overhead figures 34 to 61% come from search results, not opened
cost: Large throughput cost reported for inference; extra dependency
simpler_alternative: Pin batch size and dtype and measure the evaluation repeat spread as evaluation.md already says
reason: Addresses a real nuisance but the cost is high and nothing shows a benefit for training or small-model evaluation
cheap_local_trial: Evaluate one checkpoint at two batch sizes with and without it and compare the spread and the wall time

what: Fully fine-tune a few modules and apply LoRA to the rest for post-training
problem_here: Reference says PEFT variants land within 1 to 2 percent of LoRA after LR tuning
mechanism: Selective full-rank capacity where LoRA is weakest
evidence: arXiv 2605.18822 per search results only (not opened): Qwen-2.5 1.5B, GRPO and GSPO, self-reported +4.36% over the best PEFT baseline; no replication
cost: Extra memory for the full-tuned modules
simpler_alternative: Plain LoRA with a per-arm LR sweep
reason: Self-reported and unopened; conflicts with the kit's own tuned-variants finding
cheap_local_trial: Open the paper, then run it as one arm in a per-arm LR sweep against tuned LoRA on the project's task
